extracted.intended_audience: general adult readers of Esquire / readers interested in celebrity profiles and entertainment journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Long-form magazine feature focusing on a celebrity subject that combines scene-based lede, anecdote-driven reporting, physical and career detail, and the writer's evaluative voice to shape a portrait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-based lede that immediately reveals personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin in a concrete, present-tense scene that positions the reader with the writer and subject (e.g., 'You're sitting across from Miles Teller at the Luminary restaurant in Atlanta and trying to figure out if he's a dick.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses second-person vantage and an arresting question/hook to introduce tension; the example uses a provocative characterization to set tone. Anti-pattern: dry background summary as first paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, telling anecdotes to show character
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short, memorable stories or incidents that illuminate the subject (e.g., the champagne-coupe anecdote, the DM to Kobe, telling the waitress the highball glass is modeled after his cock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotes should be concrete and specific so readers infer personality rather than being told it. Examples in the piece: DM to Kobe, the highball comment, BottleRock clip. Anti-pattern: relying on generic descriptions like 'he's arrogant' without illustrative episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix admiration and critique — show complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the profile to both praise and critique the subject (e.g., 'So yeah, he is kind of a dick. But the thing is, you agree with him: His admittedly limited body of work so far...is pretty great.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present contradictions rather than flattening the subject into a single judgment. Use the writer's voice to negotiate sympathy and skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include physical detail and wounds to humanize
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe appearance and scars or injuries that offer backstory and vulnerability (e.g., scars from a 2007 accident, crooked nose, fleshy eyelids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical description should be sensory and tied to narrative (scars leading into stories about friends and accidents). Anti-pattern: shallow celebrity-glamor copy that omits humanizing flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronicle career with concrete roles, earnings, and trajectory
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay out the subject's filmography and career milestones with specifics (titles, years, notable performances, and even reported pay: Rabbit Hole $5,000; Spectacular Now $7,000; Whiplash $8,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize current status by comparing early indie work to mainstream projects and noting awards/recognition. Use specifics rather than vague career summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotes and dialog to convey authentic voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely heavily on the subject's own words and conversational exchanges (e.g., 'I can't cut this.' 'Do not rape' request for Uber).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should capture the subject's cadence and attitude; intersperse dialogue with brief narration to keep scene motion. Anti-pattern: paraphrasing all speech and losing the subject's voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an irreverent, magazine-appropriate tone (including profanity when apt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a candid, sometimes profane voice that fits the magazine's persona (multiple uses of 'fuck', 'dick', 'dickishness').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone must match publication and audience expectations — here, flirtation with insult and brash humor reinforces characterization. Avoid gratuitous profanity that doesn't serve characterization or risk alienating readers inconsistent with outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize subject via comparisons to peers and influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare or contrast the subject with other well-known figures to clarify ambitions and stylistic lineage (e.g., rants about Leo, Bradley, Jake Gyllenhaal, Tom Hanks, Christian Bale, Joaquin Phoenix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparisons to illuminate career goals and perceived place within an industry tradition. Provide enough explanation so comparisons aren't name-dropping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose contradictions and vulnerabilities to complicate persona
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight moments where the subject undermines his own bravado (defensiveness about hair, insecurity about looks, dating younger model, admitting to limitations like 'I literally have four teeth').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtapose bravado and fragility to produce empathy: small behaviors (asking you to cut his meat) can be revealing. Anti-pattern: one-note celebration of celebrity without private contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a narrative arc with setbacks and ambitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell a story across the piece that includes losses and forward motion (friends' deaths, lawsuit over accident, losing a role in La La Land, plans to produce his own films).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A profile should feel like a story with stakes: past trauma, career disappointments, and present plans provide dramatic throughline. Avoid list-like recitation of facts without narrative connective tissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use small sensory moments and cultural color for texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Include tactile or sensory details and pop-culture moments to enliven prose (pork belly that's hard to cut, milk tea at M2M, BottleRock dance clip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These moments make the subject tangible and situate them in a cultural moment. Overuse can feel like filler; choose moments that reveal character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate contemporary media references and controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention viral clips, TMZ, social-media behavior, and current controversies (e.g., TMZ BottleRock footage, Uber sexual-assault news) as part of the portrait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such references to show how subject is perceived publicly and how they respond to scrutiny. Be careful with legal/ethical framing when citing allegations; report factually.

rubrics_metrics.name: End with a forward-looking, character-affirming closing
rubrics_metrics.description: Close on a concise image or line that gestures toward the subject's future or enduring quality (e.g., he goes off 'to contribute to the cache or catalog or canon' and 'charm the world with his dickishness').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good closer ties back to opening themes and leaves the reader with a resonant final impression. Avoid abrupt factual endings that don't echo the piece's tone.
